disclaimer: Demonstration data. All risks, ratings, owners, and dates are illustrative.

risks.title: Penetration testing outside authorized scope
risks.description: An outsourced penetration tester accesses systems, networks, or accounts not explicitly authorized in the signed rules of engagement.
risks.consequences: Service interruption, legal liability, contractual disputes, loss of client trust.
controls: Signed scope and rules of engagement
mitigation: Require written approval for scope changes

risks.title: Leakage of client company data
risks.description: Sensitive data obtained during client engagements is exposed through insecure storage, transfers, contractor devices, or accidental disclosure.
risks.consequences: Confidentiality breach, regulatory exposure, financial loss, reputational damage.
mitigation: Use encrypted client-approved storage and transfer
Define retention and secure deletion procedures

risks.title: Compromised pentester accounts or devices
risks.description: An attacker compromises a contracted tester's credentials or device and gains access to engagement tooling or client environments.
risks.consequences: Unauthorized access, stolen evidence, interruption of testing, breach notification costs.
mitigation: Monitor privileged sessions and anomalous logins

risks.title: Insufficient vetting of outsourced testers
risks.description: A contractor without adequate skills, references, or security practices is assigned to a sensitive client assessment.
risks.consequences: Poor testing quality, compliance gaps, damage to client systems, client dissatisfaction.
mitigation: Conduct technical screening and reference checks
Require code of conduct and confidentiality agreement
Perform periodic performance and security reviews

risks.title: Late or inaccurate assessment reports
risks.description: Testing results are incorrectly documented, insufficiently verified, or submitted after contractual deadlines.
risks.consequences: Missed vulnerabilities, poor remediation decisions, contract penalties, loss of renewals.
mitigation: Require peer review of critical findings
